messages:
miriam: quick pulsecheck — onboarded Hesperus LoRA merge for cust-zenith on int4 yesterday. Ran the quick-eval pack and seeing weird soft-prompt repetition and short completions on instruction prompts. not a full regress but notable.
kevin: ugh. do we have the eval diffs? can you paste the sample ids that failed?
miriam: putting a couple here, low verbosity examples
miriam: sample 42: expected longer rationale, got 1-2 token repeat
miriam: sample 87: cut off mid-sentence after ‘therefore’
sam: can you share the run command + config? maybe a batch/kv cache issue
miriam: run was: ```bash
./run_quick_eval.sh --model hesperus-lora-merged:int4 --seed 2026 --batch 8 --max-tokens 128
```
kevin: batch=8 is a bit high for int4 on that sequence distribution, could cause truncation if runtime drops tokens? also which tokenizers used for the LoRA merge?
omar: tokenizer used was the customer's patched vocab (cust-zenith-tokenizer v2). we did remap using the merge-tool, mapping file: /mnt/merges/hesperus/cust-zenith-map.json
sam: hmm tokenizer remap + int4 quant can interact poorly if special tokens shifted. try re-running with batch=1 and max-tokens=256, seed same, and enable kv-cache-check flag: --kv-check
miriam: re-run kicked off: job 2026-1715432125 (qa-bot should post)
qa-bot: deploy-bot: Quick-eval job started (2026-1715432125) — model hesperus-lora-merged:int4 — params: seed=2026, batch=1, max-tokens=256, kv-check=on
kevin: also please run a small int8 baseline on the same samples so we can diff quant impact (int8 often preserves length)
miriam: running int8 baseline now
miriam: int8 baseline results: sample 42/87 behave fine (longer outputs). so this looks quantization-related not prompt logic.
sam: could be kernel selection path for int4. tag @infra-runtime and ask for kernel/config diff between int4/int8 serving. maybe fallback to q8_0 profile or try per-channel quantization.
omar: quick thought — the merge script applied tokenizer remap after adapter merge. might be worth redoing merge with remap applied earlier (token alignment before weight fusion) — some adapters assume original idx positions.
kevin: good call. can we do a tiny A/B: re-merge applying remap-first vs remap-after then quantize int4; run 10-sample smoke
miriam: scheduling that now. I'll post the A/B artifact links when ready.
sam: also add the sample that triggered repetition to the unit prompt set, so Optimize alerts can catch if this slips in future.
miriam: added sample 42,87 to promptset "cust-zenith-smoke" in eval dashboard: https://internal.eval.redwood/ps/cust-zenith-smoke
miriam: thanks all — will update with A/B results, and we'll escalate to runtime if kernel path looks off. :thumbsup:
